testNotes:
## Assertion rules — E25

Every status the gate can produce, in one run, so the report's Asserts tab can be
asserted against something that renders all of them.
_comment: Thresholds here are extreme on purpose. This fixture's job is to render one of every
rule state — PASS, WARN, FAIL, UNMATCHED, DISABLED, INVALID — on any machine,
and a realistic limit would make the verdict depend on how fast the runner happened to be.
The scenarios run 4-up, so a threshold anywhere near the observed value would turn a
browser test into a coin toss.
This key is also doing a second job: it is an unknown key, and the round-trip guarantee
says it must survive being saved from the report.
loadValidity's target is deliberately tiny for the same machine-independence reason: the
point of the fixture is that the legacy block is FOLDED INTO assertions[] at load and the
block itself is consumed, so what the tab shows and what a save writes back are ordinary
rules with no second dialect behind them. Whether a shortfall is detected is arithmetic,
and that is unit-tested in GateEvaluationTest where no runner speed can reach it. Both
bands are declared because the block supplies no default consequence — a loadValidity with
neither warn nor fail judges nothing at all, deliberately.

assertions.description: Comfortably inside budget — the PASS row
Over the warn band, under the fail band — the WARN row
A pattern matching several samplers, all passing
Whole-run scope — no sampler to hang off

A whole-run apdex ceiling. Deliberately unreachable — apdex is bounded at 1 by definition — so the row is PASS on any machine. Upward rather than a floor: a downward band on apdex has to sit at or below 0 to be unreachable, and the validator correctly calls that out as a rule that can never fire.
An off-grid percentile — p99.9 is resolved from the retained digest, not the standard grid. Deliberately unreachable so the row is PASS on any machine.
The typo case — this sampler is not in the run

assertions._why: No id on purpose. The loader labels it assertions[N] so findings and JUnit testcases can name it, and that label must NOT be written back into the file as a real id - it is positional, so inserting a rule above it would make the name a lie.
assertions.description: An id-less rule, which the loader has to name and the report must not rename
Cannot run — the INVALID row. Logs one ERROR per run, on purpose.
Kept in the file, not evaluated
A second PASS row, so the sort and filter specs have two of them to order

samplerNotes.Slow API: Deliberately slow — the fixture needs a sampler that breaches.
